messages:
jia: Heads-up — I'm wiring INT8 model intake. Quick question: should we run full bench (1000 samples) in ingest or a lightweight smoke + deferred full bench?

mike: I'd do smoke at ingest, full bench async. ingest path needs <200ms median.

sara: agreed. smoke should cover correctness (+struct outputs), verifiable latency, and GPU mem sanity. not cost heavy.

jia: ok. What about artifact contract? Where do we store quantized binaries + provenance?

mike: put binaries in model-registry/artifacts with manifest.json. manifest should include hash, quant config, build args, source commit.

jia: can we add a minimal admit API boundary so runtime only needs manifest + weight path? e.g., admit.v2 -> {manifest_url, metadata}

sara: yes. keep manifest immutable. runtime fetches compatible-kernel table from manifest.

mike: for gating: smoke fails -> block ingestion; full bench regressions -> automatic rollback flag and alert to #eng-ml.

jia: how to define "regression"? latency + perplexity thresholds?

sara: perf delta >5% p50 or quality drift >2% (eval set). We'll need per-model thresholds in manifest or registry.

bench-bot: scheduled full bench queued: model_id=rdw-quant-2026-03-20-17; ETA 45m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mike: FYI — I'll add a shim in the intake gateway to emit a prebench token so queuing respects customer tier.

jia: thanks. follow-up: who owns the quantized build step? infra or ml-research?

sara: infra owns deterministic build infra; ML owns tuning knobs & fail criteria. split responsibilities in onboarding doc.

jia: cool. I'll sketch RFC and attach a minimal manifest schema. ping @sara @mike if anything missing.
